bio: 1974. South Korea  (Seoul)Temptation of Lines (Visual  Line)How to WorkOil, pigment and emulsifier should be mixed with each other on canvas (writing in small characters). Visible shapes and colors should be linearly spread and such lines should be overlapped so that lines and colors can be unsophisticatedly harmonized with each other on the screen.Work NoteArtistic activities enable human beings to express their originative consciousness as well as to express esthetical values instinctively. In particular, lines and colors are fundamental factors of pictures though art has been variously developed and changed.In reproductive art, a line is one of factors that express reality. A line can unlimitedly express human spirit, through direction, speed, power, length, thickness and otherwise. A line cooperates with the significance of an object or its idea, or is vitalized independently of such things. The surface to be worked by me is a methodological factor to express mental emotion, and speedy and dynamic lines have a majority. The surface is filled with such fine abstract lines and scribbled brushstroke, and so chaotic patterns are formed. Enthusiastic rhythm, made by the formativity of an object and fine lines, is to make dynamic and refined beauty. Also, the abstruseness of lines and the colorful surface are to fill my own surface with visible polite colors.A picture is the language of an artist. The world is full of words.What do they want to say? I am shutting my mouth in the world full of words, and I implant my words and wills into my pictures.I hope to make viewers personally understand sympathize with me, without description. If they look around my pictures from the right, the left and a distance or get a near view of them, with questions of why and what, they will find out the soundless words of the artist. If I explain them in detail, my works may be lost in the mists of time. But on the other hand, if they personally find out something in a picture, it will be significant and meaningful for them. The picture may be strongly impressed on their memory. I wish viewers and artists to be intimate with each other in exhibitions, and hope to make viewers aware that art is a part of daily life.

bio:
Kim HyunAh's paintings are known for their warmth and friendliness-looking at them one is reminded of illustrations from children's books. The positive outlook of her work and love of place and life are apparent in the images she chooses : in one work a street scene takes center stage, with its red and blue rooftops, sunflowers blossoming along the street, and puppies playing. This comfortable and sentimental village landscape is in stark contrast with the busy, "gray" life of the city. The artist presents us with a village in which we would have all liked to play as children, imbuing it with a fairy tale quality. Formal perspective is set aside here in favor of simple, flat composition and bold colors which combine to present an affection-ate scene of an ideal place.

Artist’s Statement_ KIM Hyun-a
When awakened, I open the window and look over the world.
Then, the scenery becomes a picture and my day begins with it. 

Feeling curious while on the bus going through alleys,
Looking back my days while walking through a road with winding turns, 
Stepping up and down stairs, I swear myself to make a better today,
Closing and opening the door, I soothe my painful heart. 

We can’t live alone. 
While confronting and getting hurt by people, we are erased and drawn again.

In the world I am also being drawn.
And repeatedly I am being erased and drawn. 

I could be a precious existence being placed in the center of someone’s paint,
But, I also could be an existence being erased easily by someone,

And I could be a window to the world to someone,
But, I could be a small brick consisting of a wall to another.

Turning around the corner, what kind of house I will meet…..
After making another turn, who I will encounter………

In the town like a labyrinth, 
Whether I come to find a way or end up wandering around……
In that way, my life and days are being drawn on canvas. 

My paintings are like a picture diary to me. Emotions I feel everyday and sceneries remained in my memory are expressed on canvas. We can’t live alone. We are erased and drawn repeatedly while confronting and getting hurt by people. Through my works, I want to show the story of mine and people. I imagine of our lives living in familiar scenery and connect the small scraps of my imagination piece by piece. If watching the town we live in, doesn’t it look like small pieces? 

As a work is completed by a myriad of repetitions, our lives go through the same procedure. While being drawn and erased, and piling up small pieces……., we are becoming complete and perfect throughout trials and errors. 

Feeling curious about the world while walking through alleys and observing various kids living under the colorful roofs……., each piece gathers elaborately to become an artwork.

bio:
I am a contemporary abstract painter, originally from South Korea and currently living in the beautiful Island of Gods, Bali, Indonesia. I received my master degree in Fine Arts from Rochester Institute of Technology in Rochester, NY, after finishing my undergraduate study in English Literature and Psychology in Yonsei University in Seoul, Korea. 

  I have always used abstract forms to capture my deep emotions and psychological flows. However, my perspectives for life and art have been shifted greatly since I started to seek truths in life 9 years ago. The seeking naturally happened as I tried hard to cope with a series of some tough life challenges soon after moving to Bali. As a result, I gradually started to infuse the spiritual dimensions in my abstract paintings. 

  Now I see my creations as more than just beautiful pieces of art. They have become to have purposes as I have become more deeply conscious over the years. They are here to touch your soul and do their divine work within you. 
 
   I also make many custom pieces that are created all individually, taliored to each client's needs and values. Each piece is the result of manifestation through me from the very seed my client plants himself/herself. 

  I hope my art to connect with people in a deeper level, going beyond the physical and psychological dimensions, so that they can re-find their inner connections that often stay inactivated subconsciously or unconsciously. That is my goal as an artist or a creator, and my own way of contribution as a life being.  

  My paintings have been collected & displayed in many corporate offices and homes around the globe. And I have been showing my work through both online and offline exhibitions. I am currently planning to have my first solo show in Bali, Indonesia early in 2022.

bio:
Seokyung Cho is a visual artist and painter whose practice centers on the relationship between nature, memory, and emotion. Her work examines how personal experiences of landscape and travel evolve into visual reflections of the self. Through painting, she translates sensory impressions and emotional traces into color, exploring the ways in which memory shapes perception.
Rather than depicting physical scenery, Cho’s paintings evoke the emotional resonance of places revisited through recollection. Her use of color and texture serves as a language of feeling — a means of transforming transient sensations into a contemplative visual experience. Each work captures the shifting boundary between inner emotion and external reality, inviting viewers to engage with the subtle interplay of perception and remembrance.
In her recent body of work, Cho focuses on the temporality of emotion — how moments of connection with nature linger within human consciousness and resurface over time. By reconstructing these impressions through sensuous color and atmospheric composition, she investigates how memory can act as both an archive of emotion and a source of renewed understanding.
Cho’s practice ultimately seeks to visualize the continuity between nature and the human psyche, positioning painting as a space for reflection, empathy, and the rediscovery of emotional presence in everyday life.

bio:
I am a painter who reflects on how we see the world, how we remember it, and how we sense our own existence. Rather than focusing on accurately reproducing objects, my interest lies in the space between what is visible and what remains unseen—the subtle gap where perception and sensation gently waver.

Life is never entirely clear, and emotions and memories resist easy definition. I embrace this ambiguity and instability, believing that what cannot be fully grasped often reveals a deeper truth about both humanity and the world. Instead of offering definitive answers, my practice seeks to leave open questions, allowing reflection and contemplation to continue.

Figures appear in my paintings, but they are not fixed or fully determined. They emerge, overlap, and dissolve, existing in a state of becoming rather than certainty. These forms are not meant to explain objects, but to serve as vessels for memory, emotion, and traces of presence. Through form, I explore what lies beneath the visible—layers of time, lingering sensations, and the afterimages of the mind.

Through the use of light, negative space, layering, and blur, I suggest that the world is not a single, stable image, but a shifting sequence shaped by perspective and moment. Empty space is not absence, but a place where thought and feeling can dwell. Within this openness, viewers are invited to recall their own memories and experiences.

For me, painting is not an explanation, but a space for contemplation—not a finished conclusion, but an open-ended question. If a viewer can pause before my work and quietly reflect on their own emotions, gaze, and sense of being, that becomes the most meaningful outcome I hope for.

About Deconstructed Grid (Degrid)

While the formalistic grid of modernism (Piet Mondrian grid) had to remove all temporality, naturalness, emotion, literary illusion, and interactivity with the outside, Deconstructed grid implodes grid in meaning by re-expressing what the formalistic grid of modernism removed on canvas. The artist (Laila) expressed deconstructed grid through Goethe’s emotional colors, which she chose out of inner necessity.

Creative Artwork Process

My Deconstructed Grid works are more than paintings; they are sculptural objects born from a tactile dialogue with material. By blending stone powder with acrylics, I build a rugged foundation that is carved and layered to create a physical relief. Much like a traditional fresco, the mineral-based composition provides exceptional durability. These pieces are archival and resilient, standing firm against environmental factors such as humidity, UV light, and temperature shifts.

bio:
Shin believes that the longing for the original state of nature is deeply rooted in the human heart. In today’s world, nature is losing its original form amid threats such as  nuclear danger, climate change, artificial intelligence (AI), and biotechnology. We are becoming increasingly distant from the original beauty that humans so desperately desire. She thinks the Earth may be enduring the fear that one day all beauty may disappear. She wonders what untouched nature might have looked like in the  first place? And carefully place our crowns in the center of splendid and pristine nature. 

Shin believes that we are the crown created to shine above all else in beautiful nature. She believes that the crown, which has  traditionally been a symbol of authority and rule, symbolizes pride and self-esteem in an idealistic sense. As she reflects on her life’s journey, the crown she gives herself is not just an ornament decorated with gold and jewels. It symbolizes giving value to every moment of life, every challenge and the process of overcoming it. This crown gives her the strength to move forward, while the sparkling shards of light around her exist to protect and brighten our path. 

Morever, we who live in a modern society are always tired of the expectations that society demands. She believes that we should take the time to let go of everything and discover nature’s original form, so that even in our busy daily lives, we should not forget that each of us has our own crown, and remind us that we are inherently shining beings. 

Artist Shin has received numerous awards,  and had six solo exhibitions. She is active in domestic exhibitions and has participated in exhibitions in the United States, Taiwan, Monaco, Japan, France, Germany, and the Philippines.

bio:
“I do not dream of the future. I embroider clumsy things upon aging ruins.”

Toyokawa is a visual artist who weaves the spiritual and physical decay, and the sense of lethargy that define South Korea in the 2020s, into a decadent tapestry.
Navigating the boundaries of graffiti, painting, and installation art, he dredges up the emotional dregs that society chooses to ignore.
In the cracks of an aging Korea, he expresses garbage, fragments, and the forgotten remnants of others.

His works are not assertions but laments — not eruptions, but submersions.
Disfigured memories, vaguely rendered subjects, and fluorescent colors chosen to simulate a forced sense of energy — these elements collide to metaphorically express the spirit of the age.
Toyokawa’s pieces evoke a subtle discomfort, and at times, are uncomfortably beautiful.


"나는 미래를 꿈꾸지 않는다. 늙은 폐허 위에 어설픈 것을 수 놓는다."

도요까와는 2020년대 대한민국이 겪는 영육의 몰락, 무기력의 정서를 데카당스적으로 직조하는 시각 예술가다.
그래피티, 회화, 설치미술의 경계를 넘나들며, 사회가 외면한 감정의 밑바닥을 끌어올린다.
늙은 대한민국의 틈새에서 그는 쓰레기와 파편, 누군가의 잊힌 것들을 표현한다.

그의 작품은 주장이 아닌 탄식이며 폭발이 아닌 침잠이다.
형체를 잃은 기억들, 흐릿하게 그려지는 피사체, '억지 텐션'을 내고자 선택한 형광색들이 뒤엉켜 하나의 시대정신을 은유한다.
도요까와의 작품들은 살짝 불쾌한 마음을 주되, 때론 불편할 만큼 아름답다.

bio:
I create scenes where emotions dwell—moments suspended between reality and something just beyond. Through a language of hyperrealism, I quietly portray the emotional topography of modern life, where things appear familiar yet subtly surreal. These are not depictions of fantasy as escape, but invitations to revisit the emotional truths we’ve set aside.

In a world where unfulfilled desires, misunderstood feelings, and unresolved emptiness often define our experience, we dream—not to escape, but to endure. My work seeks to materialize those dreams into visual form and gently return them to reality. I use precise realism to capture the surface of the world while introducing a sense of emotional dissonance through manipulated scale, softened light, and unexpected spatial relationships.

Recurring motifs include adolescent girls, companion animals, and fragments of ordinary urban life—street corners, crosswalks, playgrounds. The girl figure is not a character, but a mirror: suspended between adolescence and adulthood, she represents the incomplete self that modern individuals carry within. She stands for the vulnerable space between societal expectation and personal emotional maturity.

Beside her are animals—oversized, yet tender presences. Each one embodies an emotional need: dogs symbolize relationship and trust, ornamental fish suggest hope, and cats represent self-worth. Their exaggerated scale serves to visually articulate the weight and significance of those inner states. They are not just companions but emotional anchors—unspoken presences that offer comfort and reflection.

Light in my work is not merely illumination—it is an emotional medium. Drawing from digital visual language—lens flares, bokeh, halos, atmospheric blur—I retranslate it into paint to express the subtleties of memory and longing. The light connects disparate elements: the real and the surreal, the subject and the viewer, past and present.

The locations I paint are not fantastical. They are drawn from everyday life: familiar but recontextualized. In these recognizable spaces, subtle distortions invite viewers to project their own emotional narratives. The realism invites immersion, while the atmosphere suggests memory—blurry, tender, and open to interpretation.

I do not illustrate emotion; I suggest it. Through the tension of a hand, a sidelong glance, or a figure leaning into shadow, I try to evoke the feeling rather than explain it. My aim is to offer a still space for contemplation—a moment where a viewer may quietly reconnect with something within.

Ultimately, my paintings are landscapes of emotion. I try to dissolve the boundary between the seen and the felt, to create quiet rooms where memory, vulnerability, and inner life can re-emerge. These paintings are not statements but companions—silent presences that stay beside us, especially in the moments when we need them most.

bio:
Sungsil yun is the granddaughter of Im Kyung-Soo (임경수), known as the last royal court painter of the Joseon Dynasty. Continuing the legacy of her family’s artistic heritage, she draws inspiration from Korea’s rich traditions and cultural history.

Her mother, an accomplished artist in her own right, was selected for the prestigious Gyeonggi Art Exhibition in 1991.

Bridging the past and the present, [Your Name] creates works that honor the techniques and aesthetics of traditional Korean art while bringing them into dialogue with contemporary sensibilities. Each piece is not only a work of art but also a living thread in a multi-generational story of creativity and devotion to beauty.

Selling as: Granddaughter of Im Kyung-Soo, the last royal court painter of the Joseon Dynasty.

bio:
Life sometimes effaces terribly cruelly and always silently.
You might attempt to enter and tangle with the lives of others, but one’s life can never eternally distance itself from solitude.
Solitude and loneliness emerge only in the private space, and disappear without trace in the streets of raining starts.
Loneliness is not to be noticed, like the calendars from a random bank or insurance company, casually kept in a corner of the room without meaning,  
Whereas you may share delightful joy and happiness, you shall not share loneliness.
No, you can neither expose nor show it to anyone.
The more I attempted to share loneliness and solitude, the more uncomfortable and miserable I became.
I dressed up and yet worried what if the flush of my youth disappears and is silenced forever.
I shopped and developed a delicate taste to keep up with the latest trends, indulged in a cup of espresso at a standing bar, and tried to remember one to two hip fad words.  
In spite of the absence of the loved one, after the confessed depression of someone close and her subsequent suicide, and even when the delusions made up with empty words parade the streets, our lives quietly go on.
The unmitigated elegance of the fabulous streets often felt too unfamiliar and cruel to me. Sometimes, I was seized by the desire to identify with those streets. Sometimes, I rather wished to be the scenery in background that any one might once look, only to pass by indifferently.
When the loneliness penetrates deep into my being, I step out to the streets painted with pleasant and vivid colors.

And I think, life any how goes on.



--from the artist’s notes, 2012

bio: Someone who loves to observe and capture the beauty of everyday things, people, or places. Her paintings reflect her journey and findings across the world.

I work on the senses of 'seeing', 'seeing sense' and 'visual organ' with the focus of 'light'. 

At one time, I was extremely afraid of the concept of "death" in which the existence of visible life dissipates in the visible world, based on the artist's own parents' "absence" and hands-on experience.
This is the beginning of my attempt to communicate with the world through visual art work. My present soul and spirit, which I recognize, cannot leave my body at will.
For that reason, I realize that the ‘invisible: non-visible world’ now has a lot of influence on my life, and instead of being afraid of the extinction of existence, I try to shed new light on my life in an active manner, expressing every moment of life through five senses, "vision," "hearing," "smell," "touch," and "taste."

My work from 2012 to 2016 was borrowed from my experience as a professional cartoonist over the past seven to eight years, and I tried to communicate with the world by conducting observations on visualizations of emotional expression.

Since 2017, varied 'light' information coming through the sensory organs of ‘vision’ has been developed into research and work on the color spectrum of 'color' expression.

The beginning is the space installation work, which weaves the threads of various colors one by one to capture the color spectrum, using the entire space to create a single work of art, and the planar painting series of vaguely colored 'spectrum' color masses that might be if they're clouds, smoke, or something else.

In the flat-panel painting series, the painting work, which defines a condition as the "sense" that changes from time to time depending on the "viewer's point" toward the object by the individual experience of the audience, finally reaches "recognition" and expresses the painting work using the Korean traditional pigment, Bunchae and Jangji techniques.

Seeking of this color spectrum work, the 'Rainbow Series', soon developed into a 'Rain Drop Series’. By abstracting colorful drops of water and changing them into a minimal circular shape, I tried to visualize the five senses that could be felt at the moment when the ‘incorporeal drops’ fell vertically down, falling from top to bottom, using gold and silver powder or foil. Falling water changes the shape of objects that we used to know because of the bending caused by light. In the rain, we can feel the scent of water, feel the touch through the bounce of the water droplets, hear the thunderous sound of water, and taste the air at that moment. In the moments when the five senses are fully utilized, "recognition" makes me realize that I am alive, and defines "color" as soon as I recognize "rain water" and "raindrops" that are refracted by light and cannot be defined by any "color," depending on individual senses. Colors, sometimes distorted by gold, sometimes silver, sometimes by color spectrum, dominate the idea as if it were defined.

We go through the process of 'recognizing' the information of the subject through various sensory organs, ‘sight’, 'hearing', 'smell', 'touch' and 'taste'. In this process, we recognize ‘others’ not myself, and realize that ‘the existence of myself’ coexists through ‘being’ other than me.

I want to communicate with the audience through a series of work called the ‘color spectrum’, which is a sensory organ called "sight" that learns information of color through the bending of light and finally defines what color it is.

Currently, I am studying holograms of experimental works that reproduce the near future of AI replacing humans through new media art as well as painting and installation, and I am constantly asking questions about "how we should live" in the midst of a season when mankind is unable to return to the previous era of Covid-19, when the meaning of space and time has been lost.

bio:
Waterfall Painter _ Kim, Soonok
Representative of Korea Institute of Art Promotion & Huam Gallery Owner

Her painting by give shape to such a huge flow of the waterfall falling down with reverberating earth and sky in a huge sound of explosion, makes us entangled by the feeling to face the prodigious power of Mother Nature just like being before our very eyes. this is a product of intuition which can interpret the substance of Mother Nature as well as image's clarity which have been built up through the long time of observation. Her sense of beauty which enables the vitality of enormous Mother Nature to be condensed on canvas, and it leads to a product in the true meaning of passion, by surpassing her skills of hands. Her painting is just more than a simple visual impression. By compressing the surging of the magnificent nature on a very small screen in a very convincing way, she makes the border of painting and reality vague. This is a result of the expressiveness of high density as well as reality which is very close to object's substance. Concrete description or straight-forward expression only to the substance, its appeal is so strong. Her painting deludes us a pretense that we are standing in front of that waterfall, and it makes us feel small. Such a sentiment comes from the true acceptance of the strong persuasion of her painting

Korean art critic, Shin Hang-seop

bio:
“Just as an architect builds a house, I build homes through my paintings.”

A painting may unfold exactly as I intended—or veer off unexpectedly—but its completion always involves pouring out every residue of my inner world. It is through this process that I construct many different kinds of homes, and the Moon Jar is one of them.

As someone who finds deep happiness in painting, I often follow the emotion of ‘happiness’ itself. In doing so, I find that an abstract, immense sense of blessing—something beyond conceptual description—emerges on the canvas. I express this serendipitous encounter with blessings through color in my Moon Jar works.

The Moon Jar series began with the theme of fortune, and I continue to expand it as a series, carrying the heartfelt wish for a life filled with lasting blessings. For this reason, I hope my paintings go beyond being mere visual artworks and become vessels of good energy and a source of positive, blessed vibes for those who experience them.

GYU YEOL LEE
I became an artist in residence at Yongdusan Park Art Street in Busan in 2024.

Collecting Pieces of Time
Difference: The Relativity of Time
Gilles Deleuze's fold is an important part of deconstructionist philosophy. The inside and outside of the fold are different worlds, and the times are different. People live between the numerous folds. And people have their own folds. In other words, people have their own worlds and times. That is why time is relative for each person. My time is also relative to others. However, many people and I live in the same era. We who live in the same era live in a large fold that shares the same world. However, we live in our own folds due to our own experiences, knowledge, perspectives, and worlds. I expressed our different times with geometric pieces and light called memories. Although we live in different times, I hope that we can meet here and now for a moment.

bio: I am a South Korean photographer who has been working in landscape photography since 2013. bio:
I am a contemporary artist who draws an unconscious world through abstraction. 
My view of art is to believe that painting can heal the mind and soul, so I try psychological healing art.

____

Q. When did you first discover art, or realise you wanted to make it yourself?

I started drawing in kindergarten, I received an award at the National Kindergarten Student Competition. Full-fledged visual art activities began with digital art while majoring in visual design at university.
Through my master's degree in psychological counseling & coaching at graduate school, I opened my eyes to non-visual art at a transcendental level beyond vision and consciousness, and I entered the true art world inside me that can be connected to everyone with my soul.
At the age of 20 to 30, I did digital artworks, and after I was 40, I had a passion to do art that breaks boundaries like pop art or abstract painting, so I started painting in 2020.
The reason why I decided to draw what I met and discovered in the true art world is that I had a deep mental sharing experience with clients while studying "participatory mysteries" during my master's course in psychological counseling, and realized that this unconscious mysterious participation experience was similar to that of the art world. 
Therefore, I discovered the possibility that the person who sees my painting indirectly experiences healing through unconscious communication, and that the transfer of emotions could be achieved through the communion experience of the participatory mental world. So I wanted to convey the feelings of happiness and love, which are the themes of my painting, in an unconscious way of Psychological transformation.
Finally, when I became sensitive to psychology and spirituality, I started attempting to truly meet, discover, and capture the unconscious world on canvas.

My art is to infuse someone nonverbal with the power of the mind and the energy of life, vitality, vividness, hope and love, happiness and energy of change.
The path to finding a way to communicate and transcend relations through art is my work process.

bio:
I am an Christian artist and high school art teacher. I am married with a beautiful daughter. My works are a visualization of praises, that is, silent songs toward God in an effort to catch up traces of beings, human loneness, and tracks of time penetrating this age.  
Through my works, I wanted to deliver religious dispositions in an existential solution in order to cognize the proper realm of religion and art as a form of combination. I tried to use the principle of formative arts to express God's footsteps shedding light on this age, not to express hardened subjects and forms such as fossils.  
"Let there be light."(Genesis 1:3) God's creation is to spread light over infinite space and to build the forms and world of creatures, while artists' creation is to break phenomenal silence with light and to reveal their beings.
The structure of works has a framework of images composed of signals and symbols. Among them, points, lines and planes account for important formative principles. My works also choose abstract expression elements and geometrical structure of repetitive lines and curves, and combine forms as images of plants and animals in the whole space of canvas. I also borrowed and expressed icons in the Medieval Ages and biblical figures in the Renaissance.
In the process of working out the space, regular repetitions of lines and curves were done by impressing materials with tools, not by brushing them. This technique produced two-dimensional space on the canvas. Pleasure evoked from the labor of repetitive impressing lines is not less than pleasure of coincidence produced by paraffin dying on a unidimensional canvas.

bio: Painting for me is a very calming experience. I often find myself getting lost in my work and being unaware of how much time may pass by. I believe that my artwork expresses this feeling I have and can be seen in many of my paintings. My paintings often have many layers and color variations that help express my personality as well as tell a journey in my painting. With the multi layers it helps create a story in the painting, to see the process and get lost in all the subtle changes. My subject matter of landscapes also reflects my attitude towards life, which is living calm and peaceful. I try and choose landscapes that make me feel most connected with the environment, and makes me want to be there. By doing this hopefully the viewer will have the same connection by looking at the painting. My paintings are all mostly high key in color and value because I want to create a light and atmospheric experience. By using watercolor I can push this feeling, because the medium is also very light and transparent. Painting is very therapeutic for me and I try to accomplish this same feeling for the viewer to make them feel the same calming affect it has on me. I want to explore this concept throughout my painting career because my goal as a painter is to try and create a connection with the viewers as well as bring in some peacefulness to the world.

bio:
I remembered the sound of a long, dusty, tattered flute. Forgot when I started counting.

When count something, want to see the end of it, but I don't want to remember the count. What a contradiction! I paint to exist. For someone, it's just a painting, but not for me, at least not for me. Painting makes me think, they make me want to understand people. The accumulation of these problems makes me think about existence.

Unlike people who hide their weaknesses, art strongly shows their limitations to living beings. There are paintings that seem to be equal, penetrating, and in some cases, animated, in front of the gaze of the beings. The gaze of these beings, orphans without families, is unfortunately unique and always avant-garde towards the world. In an age of passive beings who want to survive, who need to exist, I was able to sense life through the paintings of idols, which made me think about existence, and where Flanders and his dog converged and reached, there was nothing.

They finally lay under the paint.

My world was, after all, nothing, so I was restless and wandering, and I was ashamed to face my weakness. Because I could not take existence for granted, I tried to recognize the limits of existence, the desperation to survive, in the relationship between the painting and the world, including myself, and the relationship between the phases. Therefore, by escaping from the world as I saw it, from reality to painting, from painting to digital, I was able to embrace my world as 'nothingness' itself.

It became my homework to translate my world and organize the troubles I found in my wanderings. I do not ask you to recognize the record, to acknowledge it. So, I want to be life and I want it, and I have forgotten why I want it, painting has become a tool to explore existence, and I do not hope to attribute its form to any language. I am not trying to be some kind of hero, not trying to be a saint. Just want to know the world and the many beings that pass through it.

One day, when even this shame will cease to exist, I will be able to fully understand my world, so that I can call it like a painting with life beyond existence. Paradoxically, I hope, but I do not wish, I do not calculate, but I desire the ending. Only when the flute that mesmerizes beings begins to sound monotonous, I can move forward as a writer, as a being who longs for life. Thus, my isolated self, criticizing the world and my thoughts on existence were translated into paintings, which is the limit of what I can do now. It represents life itself, which is a context, not a result.

Therefore, the existence of life means that existence is the strength to translate the world. It is a substitute for my worries about human life, but I do not hope to attribute the fruits of these worries to anything, nor do I want to glorify the eternity of existence. Therefore, I only look at it to see what direction this question I hold goes. For only in this way, as art exists, do I show the limits of myself, so that I may come to know what life as I perceive it is. With nowhere to retreat, I continue to tear apart my isolated world and seek an existence that is more oriented.

That is my picture, my world, and I seek life in infinite silence.
My will, desire, this is what makes my heart swell, and I aim for what is beyond the world.

bio:
I am a painter based in South Korea, and have been working as a professional artist since 2014. I currently work in a small studio in Suwon.

My work begins with close observation of everyday subjects—small objects, people, or landscapes within my immediate surroundings. I am particularly drawn to the relationships between opposing qualities within a single scene: light and shadow, warmth and coolness, stillness and intensity, tenderness and sharpness.

I am interested in how these contrasting elements coexist, defining and heightening one another, while at times subtly blending and connecting. Although these are physical and visual phenomena, I approach them as clues that suggest emotional and abstract aspects of human experience.

The conflicting impressions gathered through observation become the starting point for the next stage of my work. I simplify or omit certain elements, while emphasizing others in order to clarify the underlying message. Through this process of reconstruction, I aim to reveal the contradictions within myself, as well as those inherent in the world around us.

Ultimately, my paintings seek to express both the tension and harmony between these opposing forces. I hope that viewers may encounter and interpret these quiet metaphors within the scenes I create.

bio:
Hailey P : Visual Artist & Film Art Director

"A 14-year master of visual storytelling."

Hailey P is a Seoul and Bali-based visual artist with a distinguished 14-year career as a Film Art Director in the highly competitive music video and commercial advertising industries in South Korea. Having directed the visual aesthetics for top-tier brands and global music icons, she possesses a rare ability to capture and command public attention through sophisticated mise-en-scène.

Her transition to the canvas is not a new beginning, but a cinematic extension of her long-standing expertise. Her work translates the dynamic energy of film sets into static yet powerful visual narratives, offering viewers a profound sense of visceral storytelling that only a seasoned director can achieve.

bio:
explores Korean life, nature, and moments of contemplation through a fusion of Eastern and Western painting traditions.

Inspired by everyday life and the landscapes of Korea, I explore the subtle relationship between human life and nature, seeking to express the warmth, tranquility, and poetic beauty found in ordinary moments.

Through color, line, and composition, my work connects the beauty of painting that emerges from different cultural traditions, translating memories of life and the delicate sensibility of nature into a visual language.

As an art therapist, I am also deeply interested in the healing and restorative power of art. I hope that my work offers viewers a moment to pause, reflect, and experience a quiet sense of inner peace.

bio:
Past, Present, And... (A Positive Energy of Love)

The painting work drawn on the canvas consist of innumerable lines meeting each other as well as the colors overlapped with each other. It may be a plane called 'knitted pattern'.
When seen from afar, it looks like a single color, but when you get closer, you will experience an optical illusion due to the various paints overlaid only to feel an impulse of touching it.
In this series of work processes, I would recall a happy memory, and then, the memory would be projected onto the present time only to heal me.
The image of the knitted pattern would be completed, while imitation and recomposition would be repeated from my own perspective. In this process, my philosophy that "knitting is a positive energy and love" is reflected on the work. I continue to research into it to help the audience viewing my works at the exhibition to expand their emotion.

Energy, it is the source of life for everything alive.
Owing to the energy, new life would be conceived, breathing in mutual relationship with other lives.
Although invisible to our eyes, everything alive and moving gets the energy from the Sun to regenerate itself, releasing it.
Though such a process, we feel that we are alive.

I see the origin of the energy as a positive and infinite love like mother's warm womb.
I wish that the audience facing my works and exchanging their emotion with each other would be reminded of mother's love through the media of thread and knitting and thus, would have an opportunity to think deeply about the energy of life and essence of love.

bio:
Bomin Kim is a South Korean painter who explores the subtle emotional shifts and introspective moments in everyday life through figurative minimalism.
Her works often depict solitary figures facing abstract and quiet architectural spaces, symbolizing emotional thresholds and silent transitions.
With a unique balance of geometric compositions and subdued palettes, Kim’s paintings create meditative visual narratives that invite viewers to reflect on their own inner journeys.
She mainly works with acrylic and oil on canvas, blending flatness with realism to blur the boundaries between reality and the abstract.
Her art tells quiet stories — of stillness, of decision, of emotional clarity.

HANNAH.K is an abstract artist based in Seoul and New York.
Her abstractions harmonize at the interplay of unstructured certain shapes, color, and lines in the spaces that shape her uncategorized thoughts.

"We may want to shake it off, but at times, we simply grow weary and turn away. In doing so, the emotions pile up quietly in our hearts. My work begins with the contemplation of whether I should forget about my accumulated emotions and thoughts, left neglected. I aim to express the elusive and difficult-to-articulate emotions that everyone has felt at least once in their lives. 

Existence is tangible, yet intangible, and I attempt to convey the essence of these indescribable emotions through my art. 
I think there's a possibility of empathy when someone realizes that they share similar feelings with me.
The motivation behind my artistic endeavors lies in the moments when I confront my emotions or the extension of thoughts conveyed by nature. 

Starting from observation and extending to a primal movement in the heart, I hope these fundamental motions are transmitted to the audience through my works. Certainly, emotions and thoughts can be expressed through language and body language. 
However, describing accurately every emotion with the right words or sentences is not always easy. 
Since using conventional words may not be sufficient, I prefer expressing emotions through intuitive drawings. 
Therefore, I draw abstractions that can express one’s thoughts and feelings through the harmony of shapes and colors.

I hope that the audience can empathize with my drawings, which partially visualize intangible existence,
 and that this empathy leads to comfort and genuine connection."

bio:
I was born in Seoul in 1993. 
I like to paint since I was a child. I entered the Department of Plant Life and Environmental Science. I also majored in visual design in third grade. And graduated Bachelor of Agriculture and art. I'm currently working as a barista.


In art, the most different thing from before is that I am free.
While living the fixed path of Korean society, not expressing my opinion, I did not look at myself, establish or express my thoughts and opinions.
To me, which became a habit, doing art has gradually taken me out of the frame and expanded me.  That's the biggest reason why I'm drawing.  
These days, I draw the usual "I."  One day, l feel a little scared of the world, another is a good to live.
So, it seems like me to be complicated and capricious. I draw the material that is scattered around me, the things that come to my mind. I hope my work will inspire to someone and expand themselves as they work.

bio: Jaeyoun Shin is a visual artist with an MFA in painting from Savannah College of Art and Design, Atlanta (2016). Shin incorporates watercolour, acrylic, Asian paper collage, and other media to portray the fragility, sensitivity, and complexity of memories, emotions, and thoughts expressed in her works. Collectively, the paintings are interconnected mindscapes that challenge the idea of personal identity and emotion. Her works describe different boundaries of safe and unsafe environments and various senses of vulnerability. Each work intends to transform the spaces and objects from familiar to unfamiliar and lets the viewers see different relations and perspectives. Her work has been exhibited in galleries, auctions, art fairs, museums, institutions, private collections, and Atlanta Hartsfield–Jackson International Airport in Korea, India, and mainly in the United States. Shin is now based in Seoul, South Korea.

bio:
[somewhere between sensuality and madness]
An expressionless face and static pose, intense colors and somewhat juxtaposing messages
Through the artist's Persona- the character "Mimidolly",
Express humorous of instinct, sensuality, and madness.

I want you to feel the subtle emotions hidden in the character's poker face, and Imagine hidden stories through small clues.
The most personal and secret stories...


-----------------------------------------------

I am MiMi, a South Korean artist based in Seoul. My journey through life has been a diverse and colorful one, shaped by a range of experiences and a passion for creativity that knows no bounds.

I studied fashion design at Keimyung University and grew up as a professional fashion designer in ESMOD SEOUL
These formative years not only cultivated my design sensibilities but also instilled in me an appreciation for the power of visual storytelling.

After working as a fashion designer, a fashion graphic designer, a K-POP visual director, and a lyricist, I worked with people from various countries and fields at the intersection of music, fashion, and visual art.
This fusion of creative realms ignited a new passion within me.


[The subject of the painting, and inspiration]
My art draws its inspiration from the intricate layers of human nature and the concealed desires that reside within us all. Working in diverse creative roles, from fashion to K-POP, I've been deeply influenced by design elements, mass media, movies, music, music videos, and fashion. These diverse inspirations have woven themselves into the tapestry of my artistic style.

Central to my art is the character "Mimidolly," a persona with an unwavering poker face, adorned with vibrant colors and thought-provoking text. This poker face symbolizes the modern human experience, one that often conceals our deepest instincts and desires. My intention is to encourage you, the viewer, to imagine the emotions, desires, and stories that lie beneath this façade. My art, I believe, finds its completion when you, the audience, explore your own hidden emotions and embark on a journey to unlock the stories of concealed desires.


[Painting with Music]
Music is also a medium that expresses myself. I've always been driven to create, express, and share my imagination and worldview. As part of that, I released an album named "Mimidolly," here the persona in my painting plays the role of speaker and vocalist. The album, produced by DJ Fridayyy, harmoniously combines my art world with the music world.


[K POP-ART]
My works can generally be defined as NEO-POP ART even within the genre of POP-ART.

However, I want to define it as "K POP-ART" that combines K-POP and NEO-POP ART because I was inspired by the colorful, rhythmic, and pop-artistic elements of K-POP culture, and I express that K-POP culture in my works in my own style. I want to share the K-POP Culture, which many people are enthusiastic about, with people all over the world through my own genre called "K POP-ART."


[Inspiration from India]
The experience of staying in India also had a great influence on my artistic evolution. 
Before that, my art-works had more works on general concepts than my personal stories. Like love, instinct, death, madness, etc. 
This profound and spiritually charged land has inspired a shift in my art, leading me to explore themes of the universe, energy, and religion.

bio:
The name G.Ryu comes from the Korean word “지류”, meaning a tributary or branch of a river.
Just as water divides, flows, and returns to its origin, my art follows the endless cycle of life —
from nature to animals, from animals to humans, and ultimately, back to nature again.

My works explore this flow — the subtle rhythm that connects existence and disappearance, life and death, memory and silence.

A central part of my practice involves withered trees, especially dead yews that endure for decades even after life has left them.
By placing light inside these trees, I photograph them as if revealing the remaining pulse of life within death itself.
This approach began with my work in Molundae, Jeongseon, where I captured close-up images of ancient trees now gone — each scar, curve, and surface preserving the memory of what once lived.

My representative series, “Their Lives – Cameroon”, extends this philosophy from nature to humanity.
While staying among various tribes in Cameroon, I witnessed how people live with joy, tradition, and art, even amid scarcity.
Through them, I saw that life’s beauty does not depend on abundance — that happiness, like a tributary, finds its own path through the smallest streams of existence.

Through both trees and people, I trace the same truth:
Life continues to flow.
Every being, whether rooted in earth or walking upon it, ultimately returns to the great river of nature.

bio:
I was born in Korea and am a portrait artist in Korea.
My work is not simply drawing faces.
I try to capture the person’s life and story, and convey the inner self realistically.
The core of my paintings is realistic expression.
I draw people’s expressions and eyes with delicate touches.
I try to let their stories come out as they are.

I was influenced by Diego Velazquez and the 19th century Impressionist painters.
I got a lot of inspiration from their working methods.
The medium I use is oil paint.
The paint has good color development and is suitable for my work.

In particular, I have experience painting an official portrait of the President of Korea.
In that work, I did not simply paint a portrait of a person.
I tried to portray the historical significance and social role of the President.
I tried to express the story of his life with respect and longing.

My work is unadorned and sincere.
I hope that those who see the paintings can naturally connect with the characters.
They feel emotions and understand the sincerity of the characters through realistic depictions. When you understand its depth, a portrait becomes more than just a picture; it becomes a window that tells a person’s life and history.

My work is not just a ‘picture’.
It is a story that contains a person’s existence, the traces he left behind, and the time we spent together.
The people in my portraits are not traces of the past, but living, breathing beings in our memories.
education:
I go a long way and look for the best artists,
I learned the basics of art from them.

I think the essence of art is simple.

1.
We're going to do a deep analysis of the works of historical greats,
2.
Absorb it into mine,
3.
I add my own sensibility and style to my work.

There was no need for an art college in this process.
The path I took was not different from the learning method chosen by the masters of history.

bio:
Yooshin Kim, an artist based in Seoul, South Korea, started his art career from his father who is an artist. 

His works have two main themes, The Shine Voyage Series and The Bouquet Series. Also, he occasionally covers light-captured landscapes and portraits. 

The Shine Voyage Series focuses on a trace of wave of the water from a sailing yacht, and captures the water and sky’s ceaseless changing color. His The Shine Voyage Series mixes the colors directly on the canvas, not on the palette, using a single knife. This shows abundant color energy and live texture.Through his work, the audience can feel the magnificent energy.

His The Shine Voyage Series had been all sold out in 2002, 2004, 2006 ART EXPO NEW YORK held at the Javits convention center, New York. Still many fans are looking forward to seeing his work.

bio:
“An artist who weaponizes his body, shatters narratives, and sculpts rage into canvas.”

183cm tall, dips 100 reps, pulling himself up through weight and will.
He doesn’t just paint—
He turns his own transformation into an artform.

# From a frail 40kg ghost to a sculpted hybrid of mind, muscle, and message.
# From political apathy to a canvas soaked in history, chaos, and awakening.
# From ‘Frankenstein’ to ‘FREE’—his works scream, “this is not just art—this is aftermath.”

He’s not just an artist.
He’s a narrative strategist, a self-built brand, a walking, lifting manifesto.
Each exhibition is a war room.
Each piece is a grenade.
Each rep is a ritual.

“I don’t draw pictures.
I orchestrate resistance with paint, memory, and muscle.”

bio:
The theme that penetrates many series of my works is the ‘expression of my will to be free through immersion’. The immersion enables me to dominate the canvas with infinite imagination. When I was exhausted by engineering figures filling my whole head in my early days, something offered its hand to me in the last place, which was my old dream to become a painter. The dream has come true now. The meticulous engineering disposition in the past has been changed into persistent concentration on arts, and the results of the immersion have been fully represented as works. 
The canvas looks like filled with machine parts interlocked with each other. If you take a close look, however, you can see that the marginal space is regarded as more important than entities. In other words, it means that the freedom is always in the order, and it also includes rules inside. The representation of order and rules, and space and freedom is reflecting my thoughts about life as a painter. 
I want to be remembered as an artist who is always proactive for changes without settling down in the same spot. If my works in the early stage are compared with the current works, it might be difficult to guess that they have been drawn by the same artist. However, the middle process shows that they have been changed just like a word association game. The narrative including humans’ entangled relations and our history in the base part of those works, becomes the matrix of works, so it is in the same context with humans’ nature that does not change despite the ever-changing external transformation.

bio: Joung Hwang (Hwang, Haejoung) is an artist who has spent formative years in both Korea and Canada. In filling her works with lines and shapes, Hwang chooses a combination of oil paint, acrylic, chalk and ink. Through layers of different media the artist seeks refuge in repetition and familiarity. In these arrangements what the artist seeks to achieve is neither manufactured perfection nor technical mastery; the process of painting and drawing is all that remains and matters. In an empty center of the canvas one feels safe and guarded, while the endless broken lines confine the background’s infinite space, also inviting the viewer to explore her own state of imagination.

bio:
Hi, I am Okbi. I was born and raised in Korea. Okbi is my artist name, by the way. I don't like my real name as it's a bit common in Korea. As common as Becky in the English speaking world, I guess.I majored in fine art and usually paint with my iPad. The big reason being that Korea is kind of small, and the rent is high. So I tend to work with my iPad since I lack the place to store lots of materials.

Until last year, I was obsessed with so-called contemporary art, critical toward discriminations against those marginalized in Korean society. Then I met people who worked on such art while not knowing a reason why Sewol Ferry disaster happened; and also those who didn't even know why the South Korean president was impeached. I became doubtful, and these days I tend to focus on works that are more personal. I wouldn't bring out my personal "dark past," however. I had enough chance to work with my past in college.

Furthermore, I believe art should be beautiful, not dark.

bio:
Vak Dongkyun (b.1992) is an image producer based in Seoul, South Korea. His work has been displayed in numerous group exhibitions in South Korea, including at Seoul Museum of Art, the Asia Culture Center, and the Platform-L Contemporary Art Center. In March 2019, his first solo exhibition—«Universal Universe»—was presented at Archive Bomm in Seoul. In the same year, he took part in the group exhibition «Closer When Apart» in Ottawa, which was curated by Korea National University of Arts in cooperation with the Korean Cultural Centre Canada.

He studied painting for three years at Korea National University of Art in Seoul, before discovering photography during a stay abroad at the École nationale supérieure des beaux-arts in Paris in 2015. While he had worked with photographs previously, he had used them merely as templates for his realistic paintings. The efficiency of the camera as a medium ultimately prompted him to switch to photography «so as to be able to produce images of objects that are as objective as possible,» says Vak. He taught himself the technique. He has BFA and MFA degree in Fine Arts from Korea National University of Arts in Seoul. 

Working mainly within still life, Vak observes a particularly technological object using various image production methods including document, direction, and computer generation to explore the morphological narrative of subject. His multidisciplinary subjects and their intensive reproduction have won him acclaim with A New Gaze 3 - Vontobel Contemporary Photography Prize in 2019 and Mirae Artist Award in 2017.

bio: I drew pictures from an early age in order to discover the purpose of my coming to Earth. If you ask me what art is and what painting is, I'll probably answer: For me, art is about "why people fall in love with each other". The art originated naturally. The artist's goal is to recreate the many fragments of the earth with his/her own eyes and create another silent dream world. In order to convey the silent world to people and to live as an artist, he/she is still learning the world from one part of the world. The artist collects these real things and transforms them into his/her own version. The five brilliant streaks of adjacent colors and individual voices add color to the picture, influencing other colors. In order to derive the next color from one color, the artist creates a complete universe of his/her own, one by one, following the stripes of the world. Dreams continue to expand.

bio:
Zeyah Ren’s work begins with an attention to fleeting intervals in nature moments when light glides across water, when day turns imperceptibly into night, or when memory diffuses into landscape. These thresholds are brought into spaces of contemplation, articulated through a painterly language where reflection and reality quietly intersect.

Through an uncanny gaze, He seeks to perceive the subtle transformations that unfold within scenes we often overlook. By capturing riversides, forests, and skies, the work moves beyond the notion of landscape, toward realms where presence and absence, belonging and estrangement, converge.

Sun-Min LEE is a Korean gayageum player, photographer, and interdisciplinary artist whose practice explores the convergence of music and photography. Her work integrates sound, image, and time into a single artistic experience, expanding the boundaries of traditional media.
She began developing her artistic practice in Berlin in 2015 and has been based in Hamburg, Germany since 2021. Alongside her artistic work, she teaches at the Hamburg University of Music and Theatre, where she engages with contemporary approaches to traditional music and performance. Working as a multidisciplinary artist, she moves fluidly between performance, photography, and sound-based practices.

Since 2019, her photographic works have incorporated NFT-based sound elements that allow viewers to access improvised gayageum performances through smartphone interaction. This integration introduces a time-based auditory layer to the still image, transforming photography into a multisensory encounter.

In 2023, Lee Sunmin was recognized as a traditional music performer whose work bridges minimalism and neoclassical aesthetics. Her work was introduced and critically reviewed by the National Gugak Center in Korea, positioning her practice within contemporary discourse on traditional music and interdisciplinary art.

bio:
It is likely to be seen ridiculous, if artists think themselves they are too serious all the matters of their lives. It is enough to keep a diary or journal telling their real stories, and sometimes life is full of absurdity.  .
Nevertheless, a lot of what I have done just follow my individual rhythms. Performing tempo from slow to fast have been done without any probable explanation and it corresponds to an inexplicable spontaneous body response above and beyond any kind of deductive reasoning. Set aside personal reason, as many other things would be the same as the way man-made story is.

My pictures deal with the concept of lightness. More precisely, it deals with ‘lightness, or heaviness’. It may have been involved with my personal life, or my perspective to see the world, yet it is about something mortal. Remembering from what happened in my life, the  lightness visits one when one feels tremendous burden of life, and whose quality is different that of ‘emptiness’ or ‘nihilistic sentiment’ in its temperature.
My painting is grounded in the feeling of sadness, which comes from the personal life, sometimes very attached to the lightness.

bio:
Hello, I'm Choi Goeun, a painter who wants to live  with drawing. 
I'm making a work with the hope that I can ask modern people like me, who feel the importance of time alone, how they are doing for a short time. As I asked how I was doing in the painting, I realized that everyone felt the same way. That everyone wants to live feeling really alive, not just breathing. I think there are many ways to feel alive from person to person. I want to do works that will help modern people who enjoy their time alone to check their mental state for a while in their busy and difficult daily lives.

bio:
Kim, Soyeon
I have been working on various experimental 2-dimensional drawings in 
relation to pop-cultural media.
For example, my work "Sequence",and "Series-Painting" which I have 
been working on since 2000.
These works are produced in the sense and language of film.
The main concern of my work is to create a story like a scenario through 
a parody from the existing scenes of film or strategy of illusion or a metaphor.

I am concerned about the boundary of pictoral and non-pictoral situations 
which are beyond the existing practices in art and which are created to break 
boundaries.This is the result of my long experimental way of working and 
consequently this is how I come to express a story.

Through the images interwoven each other, a work of art engenders 
symbolically unfamiliar stories that are various in their meanings. 
Like a hypertext novel, that recalls a huge variety of contents 
and contexts. 
As the hypertext novel is open to a myriad of possibilities in its composition, 
the stream of its stories can be very different, depending on the selection of 
each reader. Its storylines, composed of several plots are plural and 
crossing each other, speaking simultaneously in a number of voices without 
emphasizing merely one of them. 
Furthermore, the stories allow the readers to take part creatively in the 
process of remaking the storylines in a non-orderly manner, thereby 
stimulating them to communicate diversely. My work has been continuously 
inspired  by this point with which I am chiefly concerned.

My work has no any narratives that are lineal or concrete in their structures.  
Incomplete as it is, my work relies heavily on the union and correlation of
images. In other words, my work endlessly extends in the structure of 
juxtaposing images, thereby forming the context of a story. 
Through the experimentation of dividing, juxtaposing, or connecting 
fragmental, my work tirelessly seeks to find relativeness, attaining a dramatic 
form in the two-dimensional surface. I explore the sphere of human spirit and 
our way of life by the exploitation of the numerous images closely 
coexisting with us.  
Paying attention to these essential inseparable relationships, I try to 
reconstruct universal imagesexisting in my work.

This shows a  fragmentary image of contemporary society, at the same time 
it conveys my personal view.

"Kim Soyeon's work reveals a world hidden behind a reality intervening 
and interrupting our daily lives like an uninvited guest. 
It is not a world where everything is clear and approved, but a world
of pains, doubts, uncertainty, fear, and hysteria.
Not a world of light,made up of optimism and clearness, but a shadowed
world as it is in a nature.
The strength of Kim Soyeon's work lies in the fact that a fear dose not appear
as an ultimate darkness,but oscillates where the darkness and light co-exist.
And this is the reason why as it is in classical horror or crime films a 
psychological tension is experienced from her work.
Such conditions come to us as a lyrical beauty, and this is because her work 
dose not provide a huge answer about know truths, but tells a story of fragile
and unstable state of a human existence.
The belief of a certain existence, but the fact that the subject is still unknown, 
she tells a story about such condition in a language of doubts and uncertainty."

Eunjoo Lee(Curator)

bio:
“I love me and I love my line.”

To visualize repressed and restrained life that women go through, I used the image of the corset as a symbol. By combining the image of corset and “Jeogori”, which is Korean traditional jacket, I tried to express the harmony of those two symbols with line drawing. In an abstract expression, I expressed the harmony of line and face through soft curves and sharp random traces on the canvas or hemp.
Through the shape of flying corset, I expressed the women’s effort to escape from the restrictions. I want to give you a message about women’s desire to establish self-awareness and willingness to fly above the sky without any limitation. Engraved the shape of corset and collaged them on the canvas, added texture through modeling paste and then colored them in detail.

bio:
The Layered Traces of Space: Where Memories Intersect

I find a profound sense of liberation in being a stranger in an unfamiliar place. In travel, the weight of a memory is rarely determined by the duration of time spent in a space; instead, it is defined by the fleeting emotions and external fragments that linger long after we leave. Even when we share the same "here and now," our memories diverge, leaving behind invisible traces that are entirely unique.

My work is an exploration of these traces. I gather curiosities and lingering fragments of "space," using the perspective of my present self to imagine the memories of others. On the canvas, I fragment and layer colors to overlay new narratives onto memories that are gradually fading.

The juxtaposed colors on the screen each hold their own territory. At times they harmonize in perfect stillness, and at others, they clash and divide. This visual language serves as a metaphor for our collective existence: a tapestry of diverse individuals, each carrying distinct thoughts and experiences. Through this interplay of color and space, I invite the viewer to witness how these differences eventually find a way to coexist and blend into a singular, vibrant harmony.

bio:
Hyojin Kim is a Tokyo-based sculptor whose practice centers on metal casting as a means of exploring tension, balance, and the physical limits of the human form. Moving fluidly between traditional craft and contemporary production, Kim dissolves the boundaries between hand-driven processes and industrial techniques to develop a distinct sculptural language.

Her work is composed of interconnected human units that accumulate into complex structures, evoking states of suspension, resistance, and equilibrium. These forms emerge through an intensive, iterative process in which repetition, gravity, and material behavior play a central role.

Working across a wide range of casting methods—from beeswax and pine resin modeling to ceramic shell, gypsum, and vacuum casting—Kim integrates multiple temporal and technical layers within a single body of work. By maintaining full control over each stage of production, she establishes a direct and evolving dialogue between material, process, and form.

Her practice continues to expand internationally, with a growing international presence, including exhibitions in Europe and the United States.

bio:
Pia Jaeyoon Kim is a textile artist from South Korea based in Europe. Her practice centers on soft sculpture using wool and fibers to explore themes of contact, otherness, and the boundaries between self and non-self.

Drawing from her background in textile studies and teaching experience in fabric design and dyeing, she approaches material as both structure and language. Her works often take on organic, tentacular forms that evoke unfamiliar, speculative organisms, suggesting an alternative ecology shaped by touch and sensation.

Kim’s recent projects develop a continuous narrative world in which soft, fragile materials construct resilient and complex bodies. Through accumulation and entanglement, her sculptures embody a tension between comfort and unease, intimacy and intrusion.

She has participated in exhibitions across Europe and continues to expand her practice through research-based and experimental textile work.

bio:
Through minimalist compositions and carefully controlled light, Kim abstracts architectural forms into quiet yet charged images. The repetition of geometric structures and glowing surfaces evokes both monumentality and fragility, revealing a tension between material excess and emotional emptiness. While her work reflects a critical awareness of modern civilization and its systems of value, it does not simply condemn them.

Instead, Kim seeks subtle moments of hope within the artificial cityscape. Light functions not only as a symbol of consumption and spectacle, but also as a fragile sign of human longing and possibility. Her paintings invite viewers to pause and reflect on the psychological and emotional conditions of contemporary life, suspended between desire, isolation, and quiet optimism.

bio:
Through my work, I strive to convey empathy and healing. The act of creation, along with the conversations sparked by my art, has allowed me to confront and release emotions once buried deep within. Over time, these experiences have enabled me to gradually break free from the mental torment that once felt like an inescapable hell during my childhood. It was then that I came to realize—art is not simply about crafting objects; it possesses the profound power to heal, to transform, and to inspire change.
​
This is why I believe my story is not mine alone. In the end, <my> story intertwines with <our> story. Through my work, I hope to bring forth the emotions that lie hidden within us all.

The trees that frequently appear in my work represent both myself and all of us. These trees have no roots.
​
As a child, I saw myself as a deeply rooted tree, unable to move. The thought of leaving a familiar place required immense courage, and at that time, I was a coward. I feared change and challenges, clinging stubbornly to stability.
​
One day, I embarked on a journey alone. That day, as the wind swept across my entire body, I felt a newfound sense of freedom. For the first time in my life, I felt as if I were truly breathing. It was then that I realized—I was not just a tree, but a tree that could fly like a bird. Rootless, yes, and swaying with even the slightest breeze, yet free to stand tall wherever I wished.
​
-
À travers mon travail, je cherche à transmettre l’empathie et la guérison. Créer, échanger avec les autres à travers mes œuvres, m’a permis d’exprimer et d’affronter des émotions profondément enfouies. Avec le temps, ces expériences m’ont aidée à m’éloigner naturellement de la souffrance mentale qui, dans mon enfance, me semblait un véritable enfer. C’est alors que j’ai compris que l’art ne se limite pas à la création d’objets : il a le pouvoir de transformer, de provoquer un changement.
​
C’est pourquoi je suis convaincue que mon histoire ne m’appartient pas seulement. En fin de compte, <mon> histoire s’entrelace avec <notre> histoire. À travers mon travail, j’espère faire émerger les émotions enfouies en chacun de nous.

Les arbres qui apparaissent souvent dans mon travail me représentent, ainsi que nous tous. Ces arbres n’ont pas de racines.
Enfant, je me voyais comme un arbre profondément enraciné, incapable de bouger. Partir quelque part me demandait un immense courage, et à ce moment-là, j’étais une lâche. J’avais peur du changement et des défis, préférant m’accrocher obstinément à la stabilité.
​
Un jour, j’ai entrepris un voyage seule. Ce jour-là, j’ai ressenti, à travers le vent caressant tout mon corps, une liberté inédite. Pour la première fois de ma vie, j’ai eu l’impression de respirer pleinement. C’est alors que j’ai compris : j’étais un arbre capable de voler comme un oiseau. Sans racines, certes, et fragile face à la moindre brise, mais aussi libre de me poser où bon me semble.

bio:
Core Riddle

A Painter Who Reveals the Invisible Truth
Stories Beyond Art, Records from Parallel Universes

Inspired at the age of twenty by Kant’s words — “the starry sky above me and the moral law within me” — artist Core Riddle has long pursued a creative journey driven by wonder and inquiry.

Since his teenage years, he has explored science and philosophy, religion and mythology, art and human nature. From the observer effect in quantum physics and the theory of parallel universes to the Book of Changes in Eastern philosophy, his wide-ranging studies have become the foundation of his art.

Core Riddle’s paintings transcend the notion of mere “beautiful images.” They become maps of thought — visual records that seek to reveal the essence of both the universe and humanity.

bio:
Surrealism, Abstract artist
Based in South Korea
Artist’s Statement

My work begins with contemplation—constantly thinking and questioning the nature of existence.

Among the countless beings that make up the world, I focus on human existence, or Dasein, and explore what it means to live as the most ideal version of oneself. That is why my work, from start to finish, is rooted in thinking and being.

The ideal form of existence is based on existentialist Dasein: turning inward to seek answers, contemplating deeply rather than blaming external forces, and continuously striving for growth through phenomenological thought.

More than anything, sincerity and a sense of direction—having a purpose in life—are what define the ideal existence to me.

I needed a purpose to survive, to live. I have pushed forward, focusing only on that purpose, striving to bring ideals into reality, breaking free from my present circumstances.

At one point, I believed this was natural, even inevitable. But as I navigated relationships within society, I realized that not everyone sees it this way.

Many simply let time carry them forward. More often than not, people abandon their ideals because of reality. They blame others. They blame society.

Now, for many, giving up on ideals to continue living has become more natural than chasing them in order to survive.

So, after discarding everything, what do they live for?

In this irony, what do today’s Dasein, who have let go of the future, look toward? And how do those who still burn with dreams within the gray city manifest their existence?

This question forms the core of my artistic philosophy.

Through my work, I depict the internal and external states of Dasein who still dream of something beyond the present. I capture the lives they lead—not just as artistic subjects but as beings in themselves. By layering various materials, I give time a tangible presence in my work.

These layers of time do not follow a simple past-present-future structure. Instead, they unfold as deep past – past – present.

In this way, each piece is not just an artwork but a presence—existing in the here and now, living within reality.

bio:
I am an artist who works with the hope that my work will become a window in people's hearts and that those who see it find relaxation and rest in life.
For me, light is warm and always used as a comforting material.
The shadow created by the light is fully contained on the bowl created by the earthenware maker. The shadow originated from plants or nature and can be recognized as a meadow, or a peaceful place I imagine. This is a familiar but not easily recognized material in everyday life, and humans in nature coexist together, and the grass moving by the breath of organic and scattered winds feels as if people's impatience is subdued or they are out of a competitive modern society.
By placing ceramics bowls and cups that resemble human life in the work to contain light, it creates the feeling of being in a calm place given by nature. Drawing a time fully expressed as myself, I draw a work that becomes quiet and calm when drawing after fierce competition in life. It is as if he lives a therapeutic life in which heals himself through the heart of wishing that the life in the work will be the present life and the act of drawing the work.
The small children appearing in the work can be felt as an element of directing that allows those who live in a peaceful place to enjoy more happiness there, and the artist's spokesperson or viewers can easily project it and enjoy the calm peace in the work.
Through light and vessel, the artist shares a comfortable and warm world different from reality in the work, and the work the artist talks about becomes a window in the viewer's mind and expresses it with another light. I hope that the moment you appreciate the work, you can feel the healing and peace that the artist speaks.

bio:
Yang Ji-song is a painter who tries to capture the light of life even in the darkness.
The artist felt that he was growing through the journey of overcoming personal wounds and finding out who he is, and he expresses that process and realization through his paintings.
The artist is interested in unchanging and unchanging truths, love, happiness, vitality, nature, theology, and musical elements, and visualizes the recovery and self-awareness of the human mind using materials such as acrylics and pens.
Yang Ji-song's works contain strong vitality and fluctuating emotions. The artist's ultimate goal is to find himself through his paintings and further to make the viewer feel happiness and the feeling of being alive. I hope that everyone who encounters Yang Ji-song's paintings will look deeper into themselves and be healed.
